data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 narrows the comparison to AI-operated services trained on identical public datasets, but the problem statement concerns general independently-operated services vs. a large service with strictly more internal redundancy. By assuming the small services are algorithmically homogeneous and the large service is diverse, it sidesteps the actual comparison rather than arguing it. The counterconditions concede that locally generated private data breaks the mechanism, yet the problem makes no such restriction; with heterogeneous implementations (independent code stacks, configs, data), a decentralized network can have genuine failure-mode diversity. The 'strictly more internal redundancy' in the large service does not grant epistemic diversity unless assumed, and the large service can itself share a common training set across sub-services; thus SRC_001 does not show decentralized architecture is strictly less resilient on the terms posed.
